purpose: Records why each supply family is treated as permitted for resale, so route-level termsStatus is traceable to something rather than being an unexplained constant.

howToRead.permissionBasis: The only three values are supplier_confirmed (the supplier's own governing document permits this resale model, or the supplier confirmed it in writing), owner_operated_documented (we operate the supply ourselves and the basis is recorded here), and unresolved (the governing document was not obtained, is silent, or restricts resale). unresolved is not a soft yes.
howToRead.resaleAllowed: This is the OWNER'S OPERATING DECISION to sell the route and carry the commercial risk. It is NOT a statement that the supplier has permitted resale. Read permissionBasis for that. A family may be resaleAllowed true and permissionBasis unresolved at the same time; that combination means the owner is selling without established supplier permission.
howToRead.restrictionFound: A clause in the governing document that on its face restricts what we are doing. Quoted rather than summarised. Non-null means an owner decision is required.
howToRead.notLegalAdvice: Every reading here is a plain reading of a public self-serve document retrieved on the recorded date. None is a legal opinion. A negotiated or enterprise agreement held by the owner may say something different and would supersede these readings.
howToRead.providerNamesPublic: false across every family: we may sell these routes but must not publicly name which supplier backs which route, so no public surface may render supplierTermsUrl or providerId.

summary.liveRoutesOnUnresolvedPermissionNote: 0 because the commercial gate now pauses them. Before the gate, 18 routes were live on unresolved permission; that is the condition the gate closed.

Selling metered API access to Workers AI inference is on its face selling access to the Services to a third party.

families.restrictionFound: Section 2.4(d) prohibits 'Resell, redistribute, or make available any portion of our Services on a stand-alone basis', with a carve-out permitting integration into the customer's own Application 'provided that your Application contributes material independent functionality beyond our Services'. Our ai.speech route is a metered pass-through to synthesis and does not currently contribute material independent functionality, so it reads as the prohibited stand-alone case rather than the carve-out. Section 2.4(i) separately bars use of Output for benchmarking or competitive analysis.

families.restrictionFound: Master agreement section 3.3(c): Customer will not 'sell, resell, sublicense, transfer, or distribute any or all of the Services'. A metered pass-through endpoint to a Vertex model is selling the Service.

This is a real contractual carve-out, not an inference, and it is the path by which these routes could become permitted. It does not apply to a thin pass-through, which is what the current ai.chat / ai.image / ai.embed routes are.

unresolved: No family is supplier_confirmed. Four of five are unresolved, and three of those carry an explicit restriction on their face: Cloudflare master agreement 2.2.1, Deepgram 2.4(d), and Google Cloud master agreement 3.3(c). Only Groq has no restriction read against it, and only because its governing agreement could not be obtained at all. A consistent pattern emerged across all four suppliers: reselling raw inference as a metered pass-through is restricted, while integrating it into a product with material independent value is permitted or carved out. Google 1.1 and Deepgram 2.4(d) state that carve-out in nearly identical language. That makes this a product-shape question as much as a paperwork question: the current routes are thin pass-throughs, which is the restricted form under every agreement we have read. All eighteen routes are therefore paused on the commercial gate, none is sellable, and no engineering check was weakened to avoid that outcome. resaleAllowed remains an owner operating decision and is not read anywhere as evidence of supplier permission.

resolutionPassOutcome.vertex: A restriction was found rather than a permission: master agreement 3.3(c) prohibits reselling the Services. Section 1.1 carves out integration into an application with material value independent of the Services, which is a genuine contractual path but does not cover a pass-through. The Service Specific Terms section governing generated output could not be retrieved after four attempts; the page truncates before the AI sections every time.
resolutionPassOutcome.groq: Blocked, not resolved. The governing Groq Services Agreement is not publicly retrievable: two candidate URLs are website-scoped and expressly exclude cloud service use, one 404s, and a web search returned nothing. Requires owner account access.
